subject.title: fix(config): improve validation error messages with line numbers, bracket paths, and received values

question: What disclosure contract should terminal config errors use when the source literal differs from the effective value after includes or environment substitution?
rationale: Source literals can be inaccurate, while effective values can expose substituted secrets; code inspection cannot choose that user-visible security boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Gate Effective Hints
options.body: Show the effective rejected value only when provenance and sensitivity checks prove it is the same safe non-secret literal, and omit `got` otherwise.

options.title: Label Source Values
options.body: Display only the raw source literal with explicit wording such as `source value`, avoiding the claim that it is what validation received.

options.title: Remove Value Hints
options.body: Land line numbers and bracket paths without received values, retaining the lowest-risk portion of the improvement.

recommendation.title: Gate Effective Hints
recommendation.body: Show the effective rejected value only when provenance and sensitivity checks prove it is the same safe non-secret literal, and omit `got` otherwise.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses canonical config snapshot semantics and terminal disclosure policy in recently maintained config code.
